definition: An AI system that carries out tasks step by step on your behalf, such as searching, filling in forms or drafting documents, rather than only answering questions.
What it costs to get a job done with an AI model, which depends on both the price per word processed and how much work the model needs.
Government rules that limit which countries or companies may buy certain technologies, such as advanced AI chips.
When a large platform adds a feature for free that smaller companies were selling on its own, often putting those companies out of business.
An AI assistant that notices what needs doing from your email, calendar or files and offers to do it, instead of waiting for a request.
Software that runs on an organisation's own servers or cloud account, so its data does not pass through the vendor's systems.
AI models and computing that a country hosts and governs itself, so that data and control stay under national rules.
Testing of an AI model by an independent organisation rather than by the company that built it.
How well a person's trust in a system matches how reliable it really is: trusting it when it is right and doubting it when it is wrong.
